about.intro_content: Prof. Sheng-Ping Li is a Professor in the Department of Pancreatobiliary Surgery at Sun Yat-sen University Cancer Center (SYSUCC), Guangzhou, and a renowned surgical specialist in pancreatic and biliary cancer treatment in China.
about.detailed_content: Prof. Li completed postdoctoral research training in the Cancer Center at the University of Michigan, USA, in 2003. His work focuses on multidisciplinary treatment of pancreatobiliary cancer and its effects on the tumor immune microenvironment, including tumorigenesis and factors affecting disease development and prognosis. He has contributed to multicentre research distinguishing pancreatobiliary-type ampullary adenocarcinoma from cholangiocarcinoma using multimodal data analysis, and leads clinical trials evaluating adjuvant chemotherapy regimens for gemcitabine-refractory pancreatic cancer after curative resection.

faq.section_heading: Frequently Asked Questions About Prof. Sheng-Ping Li

items.question: Does Prof. Sheng-Ping Li accept international patients?
items.answer: CancerFax can coordinate medical report review and consultation support for international patients seeking an opinion related to pancreatic or biliary cancer at Sun Yat-sen University Cancer Center, subject to hospital availability and case acceptance.

items.question: What is Prof. Li's area of specialisation?
items.answer: Prof. Li specialises in the multidisciplinary treatment of pancreatic and biliary cancer, including surgery and research into the tumor immune microenvironment.

items.question: How can I request a consultation or second opinion?
items.answer: Submit your medical reports through CancerFax. The CancerFax team reviews the documents, prepares the case for submission, and coordinates next steps with SYSUCC's International Medical Center, subject to availability.

items.question: Is Prof. Li involved in clinical trials for pancreatic cancer?
items.answer: Yes. Prof. Li is Principal Investigator on a multicentre trial evaluating second-line adjuvant chemotherapy for gemcitabine-refractory pancreatic cancer after curative resection.

items.question: Does Prof. Li treat ampullary adenocarcinoma?
items.answer: Yes. Prof. Li has contributed to research distinguishing pancreatobiliary-type ampullary adenocarcinoma from cholangiocarcinoma, helping refine diagnosis and treatment approaches for this cancer type.
